chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, who said: I heard him say:

Indeed, the servant stands in prayer at night, and sleep overcomes him, causing him to sway to the right and left, with his chin resting on his chest. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commands the doors of heaven to be opened, and He says to the angels: 'Look at My servant; what is befalling him in his striving to draw near to Me through what I have not made obligatory upon him, hoping from Me for three things: a sin that I will forgive him, or a repentance that I will renew for him, or sustenance that I will increase for him.' So I call you, My angels, to witness that I have gathered all three for him.

key_terms.التَّقَرُّبِ: Striving to draw near to God

ai.seo_question: What are the three rewards Allah grants to a servant who prays at night while sleepy?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the immense divine attention granted to the worshipper who perseveres in night prayer despite the physical struggle of sleepiness. Allah commands the gates of heaven to open and instructs the angels to witness a unique divine decree where He simultaneously grants forgiveness, renews the servant's repentance, and increases his sustenance as a reward for voluntary devotion beyond obligation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 7.  The narrator says, “I heard him say that if one gets up at night after turning to his left and right in such a state that his chin is touching his chest (out of tiredness), Allah orders the doors of heavens to be opened and says to His angels: ‘Look at this servant of Mine. He is going to perform what is not even obligatory for him. He can expect three things from Me – that I forgive all his sins, I give him a chance to repent once again and increase his earnings. I hold you all angels as witness that I would grant all these things to him’.”
